action: Telecom providers in Germany should prepare a process to receive and act on traffic-data preservation orders from the BfV and BND. Other firms with German operations should have legal teams read the final text once promulgated.
exec: German intelligence agencies gain offensive cyber and wider surveillance powers; telecom providers face new orders to preserve traffic data.
plain: Germany's parliament passed a law letting its foreign spy agency hack back against foreign attackers and giving its domestic agency wider surveillance powers, with an independent council approving orders in advance.

key_findings: The Bundestag adopted the bill in the committee's amended version by 308 to 190 with 71 abstentions; CDU/CSU and SPD backed it, AfD and Die Linke opposed.
The BND may act proactively against concrete threats from foreign powers, such as sabotaging attackers' systems or shutting down state hacker servers.
The BND may keep unreviewed content data up to six months and metadata up to twelve months.
The BfV gets limited covert intervention powers without coercion against persons, plus device access, biometric image matching and AI tools.
The Independent Control Council takes over prior review of orders and data protection oversight; a bill to strengthen parliamentary control is promised next year.
recommendations: Telecom providers must comply with preservation orders from the BfV and BND to freeze traffic data until disclosure conditions are met.
Agencies must obtain prior review of orders from the Independent Control Council and report to the Parliamentary Control Panel.

summary: The Bundestag passed the government's intelligence services reform on November 13 by 308 votes to 190 with 71 abstentions. The foreign service BND may act against concrete threats from foreign powers, for example by sabotaging attackers' systems or shutting down state hackers' servers. The domestic BfV gains narrower covert powers, device access, biometric image matching and AI analysis. Both can order telecom providers to freeze traffic data.
title: German Bundestag passes intelligence law reform giving BND and BfV active cyber powers

validation.note: Reviewed against the original German Bundestag document (plenary record page); the bill text itself was not read.
